key_insight: A distributed QAOA-plus-classical-repair pipeline can scale constrained quantum optimization to a 1,710-variable matching problem by partitioning it into hardware-executable subproblems.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route for applying near-term quantum processors to large network optimization tasks such as grid scheduling and energy trading.
method: Spectral graph partition the large matching problem into smaller qubit-sized blocks.
Run single-layer QAOA sampling within each partition on hardware or simulation.
Use E-FCFW plus greedy feasibility repair to assemble valid global decompositions.
evidence_signal: On PEGASE-1354, repaired QAOA samples outperformed simulated annealing and uniform random sampling, and spatial circuit packing cut hardware execution time by about 3×.
watch_item: Performance depends on partition size and retained quantum correlations, so overly small partitions or aggressive MPS truncation can degrade solution quality.
paper_title: Scaling Quantum Optimization to the Thousand-Qubit Scale with Distributed Quantum Sampling
